summary: Ran public API and UI smoke/e2e coverage for patient and doctor flows. Auth, discovery, booking, Gemini brief, private patient queue data, cancellation API, doctor settings, Dai streaming, and responsive rendering passed.

critical.issue: Doctor registration sets approved=false but login/current-user still grants access to the doctor dashboard; no invite/admin approval gate is enforced.
WebSocket accepts unauthenticated connections and stores every connection globally; broadcast sends each doctor's queue snapshot to all connected sockets, leaking queue data across doctors.

minor.issue: No reschedule endpoint is implemented; only booking and cancellation exist.
No brute-force lockout after five failed attempts is implemented.

integration_issues.issue: Queue screen control only displays a toast saying cancellation is available; it does not cancel, reschedule, or open appointment details.

integration_issues.flow: Live queue updates and browser alerts
integration_issues.issue: Frontend uses five-second polling in doctor dashboard and no WebSocket connection or Notification API; required live updates and 15-minute/next alerts are not wired.

action_items: Enforce doctor approval/invite before login and role dashboard access.
Authenticate WebSockets and scope connections/broadcasts by doctor_id.
Implement patient reschedule/cancel UI backed by APIs.
Wire frontend WebSocket updates and in-app/browser 15-minute and next alerts.
Add brute-force lockout and auth regression coverage.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend never connects to the required WebSocket endpoint despite backend exposing one.
The global connections set makes queue broadcasts cross-tenant; this is a privacy issue.
seed_data_creation: Created and cancelled one TEST-style patient booking through the public API/UI; no persistent seed users created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Patient and doctor seeded login credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Existing database has demo patient queue entries from prior smoke tests; retest approval, WebSocket scoping, alerts, and cancellation/reschedule after fixes.
rca of the issue: The implementation contains only a polling interval for doctor queues and the patient cancel handler is hard-coded to notify('Cancellation is available...'). Backend has no reschedule route. Doctor approval is stored but not checked by current_user/login. WebSocket connections are global and broadcast ignores doctor_id filtering.
